link.description: Link to this transaction in your Memo Bank workspace.

reference.description: Reference of the money movement. In case you initiate a transfer between two of your own accounts, both transactions (`debit` and `credit`) will have the same reference, it can be safely used to correlate them.

account_id.description: ID of the account this transaction belongs to.

amount.description: Amount of the transaction, in the smallest unit of the `currency`. The amount is always positive, use `direction` to give it a sign.

local_iban.description: IBAN through which this transaction got in or out of the account. Can be the main IBAN of the account or a virtual IBAN.

currency.description: Currency of the transaction amount, in ISO 4217 format.

request_date.description: Date at which the transaction has been requested, in ISO8601 format. Usually the same as the execution date, except for scheduled transfers and transfer requests.

execution_date.description: Date at which the transaction processing has started or will start, in ISO8601 format. For debits, that’s when the money is removed from the available balance of the account.

accounting_date.description: Date at which the transaction has been confirmed, in ISO8601 format. For credits, that’s when the money is credited from the available balance of the account.

internal_note.description: Internal note attached to this transaction, visible only in your Memo Bank workspace.

batch_id.description: ID of the batch this transaction belongs to, if any.

custom_id.description: Custom identifier attached to the transaction. It is not transmitted nor visible in your Memo Bank workspace. It can only be retrieved or used to search for transactions via Memo Bank API.

custom_metadata.description: Custom metadata attached to the transaction. It is not transmitted nor visible in your Memo Bank workspace and can only be retrieved via API.

attachment_count.description: Number of documents attached to this transaction.

settlement_amount.description: Settlement amount of the transaction, in the smallest unit of the settlement currency. The amount is always positive, use `direction` to give it a sign.

settlement_currency.description: Settlement currency of the transaction amount, in ISO 4217 format.

message.description: Message attached to this collection, visible to all involved parties.

It can be used for reconciliation or to link tasks relating to the collection. For example, if a collection is returned, its return will share the same endToEndId.
